transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my daughter and a friend made me come in because they're worried about how I've been acting, but they just don't understand. I know people think it sounds strange, but I’m certain there are forces directing my art and that this exhibit has a special destiny, no matter what anyone says.
Lately, have you noticed any changes in your sleep or energy levels, such as needing much less sleep than usual but still feeling full of energy?

Yes, I've been absolutely bursting with energy lately, waking up buzzing and staying up late into the night pacing and working on my art. I feel this intense drive to keep moving, so I barely even sit down to rest my knees because I'm afraid of losing my momentum.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt very down, depressed, or lost interest in things, or have you experienced high-energy phases like this before?

To be honest, I don't recall ever having major periods of depression or any high-energy phases like this in the past. This whole experience is completely new to me, and it feels very unique compared to how my life usually goes.
Did you start feeling that forces were directing your art before this sudden burst of high energy began, or did those thoughts only start once you began feeling so energized?

Those thoughts definitely only started once I got into this highly energized, revved-up state a few months ago. I never had any of these beliefs about invisible forces guiding my art before this period. When I do calm down a bit, those ideas seem to fade, so they're definitely tied to this high energy.
Have you ever experienced these unusual beliefs, or perhaps heard voices that others couldn't hear, during times when your energy and mood were completely normal?

No, I've never experienced anything like that when my mood and energy were normal. These ideas about forces guiding my art only started once I got into this highly revved-up, nonstop state a few months ago. When I do calm down, those thoughts fade away and I realize they are just tied to that overcharged period.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is experiencing a first-time, single manic episode characterized by markedly increased energy, decreased need for sleep, psychomotor agitation, and goal-directed activity (working nonstop on art). This is accompanied by delusions of grandeur (believing invisible forces are directing her art and that her exhibit has a special destiny). These psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the manic state, which has lasted for a few months, fitting the criteria for a manic episode with psychotic symptoms (F30.2).
